paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: at Cana, Jesus gives the very best. The wine has run out (John 2:3). Then Jesus tells the servants, "Fill the jars with water," and the water becomes wine (John 2:7, 9). The need was real, and what came out of those jars was fine wine (John 2:10).

Look at who knew, though. The master of the banquet "did not know where it was from, but the servants who had drawn the water knew" (John 2:9). The servants did what Jesus told them, and they knew where the wine came from. I think that's worth noticing, baker: the people doing the plain, simple work were the ones who knew.

And the master says it best: "you have saved the fine wine until now!" (John 2:10). Jesus doesn't hand out leftovers. John calls this "the first of His signs," and says it "revealed His glory, and His disciples believed in Him" (John 2:11). So the point is bigger than a party getting rescued. The sign shows who Jesus is, and that's why you can trust Him with whatever you've run out of.
